diagnostic_evidence.quote: \subsection{Limiting spectrum property for absorbing boundary conditions and PMLs}

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction announces two types of numerical results, the second being experiments 'on the discretised problem using the edge element method'. The numerical section contains only the single subsection on the limiting spectrum of the iteration matrices, after which the document ends with the bibliography; no discretised or edge-element results appear anywhere in the paper.

failure_location.quote: Finally in \Cref{sec:numeric} we present two types of numerical results: first, showing that the limiting spectrum is descriptive for the convergence of the algorithm even in the case of a moderate number of domains and then on the discretised problem using the edge element method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or qualify the announcement of the edge-element results in the introduction (supplying the missing discretised experiments would be new work not supported by the source).
issues.overall_effect: The paper's outline and advertised numerical coverage overstate the delivered content: the promised discretised validation of the limiting-spectrum predictions and of weak scalability is not present. All delivered formal results and experiments are themselves unaffected.
issues.title: Announced edge-element numerical results are absent from the paper
issues.why_classification: The defect concerns announced but never delivered content; the least supported repair is a local edit of the outline claim, and no delivered theorem, experiment, rate, or guarantee is invalidated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We can easily see that that the determinant of the matrix is not zero iff $k^2 - \beta^2 \neq 0$ and in this case the components $(\widehat{E}_{y},\widehat{E}_{z})$ and $(\widehat{H}_{y},\widehat{H}_{z})$ are uniquely defined.

issues.failure_explanation: The symbol $\sigma$ appears in the reconstruction system eq:syst-recov (and hence in the matrix of eq:syst-recov-2 and in the determinant claim) but is never defined anywhere in the paper; the Maxwell system Maxwell-eq contains no such term. The reconstruction system and the claim 'determinant nonzero iff $k^2-\beta^2\neq0$' are therefore formally ill-defined as written (with conductivity $\sigma$ the correct condition would be $\omega^2\mu\varepsilon+\imath\omega\mu\sigma\neq\beta^2$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\sigma$ as the electrical conductivity in the first-order Maxwell system (or set $\sigma=0$ to match Maxwell-eq); the determinant condition then reads $\omega^2\mu\varepsilon+\imath\omega\mu\sigma\neq\beta^2$ (i.e. $k^2\neq\beta^2$ when $\sigma=0$), which holds for all $i\geq1$.
issues.overall_effect: The reconstruction system and the invertibility claim of the modal analysis are formally ill-defined; the modal decomposition and all later mode-based results remain valid once $\sigma$ is defined (conductivity) or set to zero, since $k^2-\beta^2=\lambda_i\neq0$ for all modes $i\geq1$.
issues.title: Undefined conductivity symbol σ in the modal reconstruction system
issues.why_classification: A one-line local repair (define $\sigma$ or set it to zero) restores full rigor; no claim, rate, or advertised scope changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The three PML eigenvalues in eq:lambdaPML carry an overall minus sign that contradicts the paper's own derivation: def:op-PML has the positive sign and the trace of eq:dec-E-PML at x=b_j is (1 - e^{2\imath\beta(1+\imath\sigma)\ell})\widehat{\bfE}\times\bfn, so the ratio defining $\mathcal T$ is +\imath\beta(1+e^{2\imath\beta(1+\imath\sigma)\ell})/(1-e^{2\imath\beta(1+\imath\sigma)\ell}), not its negative. Equivalently, as $\ell\to+\infty$ the written formula tends to $-\imath\beta=-\kappa$, minus the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann value $+\kappa=\imath\beta$ (the value prop:added-1 itself assumes), so the DtN-limit remark is misjustified and prop:added-1's premise contradicts the written PML formula.

failure_location.quote: \widehat{\bfE}^{\rm TE,\pm}_i \times \mathbf{n} \xrightarrow{\mathcal{T}} - \imath \beta^{\rm TE}_i  \dfrac{1 + e^{2 \imath \beta^{\rm TE}_i (1 + \imath \sigma)\ell}}{1 - e^{2 \imath \beta^{\rm TE}_i (1 + \imath \sigma)\ell}} \widehat{\bfE}^{\rm TE,\pm}_i \times \mathbf{n}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the overall sign of the three eigenvalues in eq:lambdaPML to +\imath\beta^{TE}(1+e^{2\imath\beta^{TE}(1+\imath\sigma)\ell})/(1-e^{2\imath\beta^{TE}(1+\imath\sigma)\ell}), +\imath(k^2/\beta^{TM})(\cdot), +\imath k(\cdot), matching def:op-PML and the exact DtN; correct the sign of the $\lambda$ values in the proof of prop:added-1; recompute the PML figures and the PML-vs-ABC comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The PML transmission operator is defined with the wrong-signed eigenvalues; the DtN-limit remark is misjustified (the written formula tends to $-\kappa$, not the DtN), the proof of prop:added-1 repeats the wrong-signed values (though its nilpotency conclusion is sign-robust, since $a=0$ only needs $\lambda^2=\kappa^2$, and its statement $\lambda=\kappa$ is the correct one), and every quantitative PML prediction (limiting spectra, figures 4-5, the PML-vs-ABC comparison) is unreliable as written. The mode-by-mode iteration theory, which is generic in $\lambda$, is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong overall sign in the PML transmission eigenvalues eq:lambdaPML
issues.why_classification: The erroneous sign is load-bearing for an entire advertised transmission condition and invalidates every quantitative PML prediction, which must be recomputed; but the repair is a contained sign fix, the formal results (generic in $\lambda$) survive, and no regime, rate type, or guarantee is lost, so no new proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we can deduce that for $\lambda^{\rm T}_i = -\imath k$: \quad a^{\rm T}_i(\kappa) = -a^{\rm T}_i\left(\frac{k^2}{\kappa}\right) \quad \text{and} \quad b^{\rm T}_i(\kappa) = b^{\rm T}_i\left(\frac{k^2}{\kappa}\right)

a^{{\rm T}}_i(\kappa) &= \dfrac{((\lambda^{\rm T}_i)^2 -\kappa^2) \left(e^{\imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (L+\delta)} - e^{-\imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (L+\delta)}\right)}{\left( \kappa + \lambda^{\rm T}_i \right)^2  e^{\imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (L + 2\delta) } - (-\kappa + \lambda)^2  e^{-\imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (L + 2\delta)}}

issues.failure_explanation: The first displayed identity is algebraically false: $k^2-k^4/\beta^2=+\frac{k^2}{\beta^2}(\beta^2-k^2)$, not its negative (e.g. $k=2,\beta=1$ gives $-12$ on the left and $+12$ on the right). Moreover the deduced fixed-$T$ functional identities $a^{T}(\kappa)=-a^{T}(k^2/\kappa)$, $b^{T}(\kappa)=b^{T}(k^2/\kappa)$ are not valid as stated; the correct relations are cross-type, $a^{TE}(\kappa)=-a^{TM}(k^2/\kappa)$ and $b^{TE}(\kappa)=b^{TM}(k^2/\kappa)$ (equivalently $a^{TE}(\beta)=-a^{TM}(\beta)$, $b^{TE}(\beta)=b^{TM}(\beta)$ at equal $\beta$), which are verified by direct substitution into the formulas of prop:R-ite. The remark's final conclusion (TE and TM iteration matrices coincide up to the sign of $a$ when $\beta^{TE}=\beta^{TM}$) is nevertheless correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the identity to $\frac{k^4}{\beta^2}-k^2=-\frac{k^2}{\beta^2}(\beta^2-k^2)$ and restate the deduction as the cross-type identities $a^{TE}(\kappa)=-a^{TM}(k^2/\kappa)$, $b^{TE}(\kappa)=b^{TM}(k^2/\kappa)$, verified by direct substitution into the formulas of prop:R-ite.
issues.overall_effect: One intermediate identity and the stated functional identities in the remark are incorrect as written; the remark's conclusion (TE/TM coefficients equal up to the sign of $a$ at equal $\beta$, hence identical limiting spectra) is true, so the numerical section's claim that $I^{TE}(r)$, $I^{TM}(r)$ and $I^{TEM}(r)$ share the same limiting spectrum stands.
issues.title: False algebraic identity and misstated functional identities in the TE/TM comparison remark
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic correction; the remark's conclusion and all downstream claims are true and survive, with no new lemma or construction required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (with convention $e^{-\imath \omega t}$ where $\omega$ is the pulsation)

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's stated convention $e^{-\imath\omega t}$, an absorptive medium has $\Im\varepsilon>0$ (equivalently $\Im k>0$): since $k^2=\omega^2\mu\varepsilon$ and modes $e^{\imath\beta x}$ decay in $+x$ only for $\Im\beta>0$, the stated $\varepsilon=\varepsilon'-\imath\varepsilon''$ with $\varepsilon''>0$ gives $\Im k^2<0$, i.e. growing waves. The paper's own experiment $k=10+\imath$ has $\Im k>0$, which is the damped case, contradicting the prose description.

failure_location.quote: which corresponds to the case of the complex electric permittivity $\varepsilon = \varepsilon' - \imath \varepsilon''$ with $\varepsilon'' > 0$. From physical point of view this means the waves are damped in an absorptive media

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write $\varepsilon=\varepsilon'+\imath\varepsilon''$ with $\varepsilon''>0$ (equivalently $\Im k>0$) to match the $e^{-\imath\omega t}$ convention and the experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The physical interpretation of the absorbing-media experiment is stated with the wrong sign; the experiment itself ($k=10+\imath$) is the correct absorbing choice, so the reported convergence improvements and the weak-scalability conclusion stand, but the prose convention is false.
issues.title: Wrong sign for the absorbing permittivity under the paper's stated time convention
issues.why_classification: A single-sign prose correction; the experiment and its conclusions are correct as performed, and no formal result is affected.
